free_tier.stated: unlimited domains per account with 20 free subdomains on each, plus 5 free hostnames on a shared registry of 23,087 domains

per_object_cap.stated: 5 hostnames on the shared registry and 20 subdomains on each domain you own, on the free plan
per_object_cap.notes: the paid plans raise the subdomain cap to 50, 100, 250 or 500 and add wildcard records, which the free plan lacks

retention.stated: a hosted domain that stays undelegated (broken) for 365 days is disabled; a shared-registry hostname lasts only while its domain stays in the registry, which the FAQ says may disappear next week

interface_detail: no general record-management API is documented, and the /api/ page is behind a login, so its content is unverified: behind a sign-up; the site's client list says a client that sends a SHA1 hash of the user name and password can fetch the needed update URL itself; the free plan's programmatic path is the dynamic-update URL https://sync.afraid.org/u/<token>/ (https://v6.sync.afraid.org/u/<token>/ for IPv6), which changes the address of an existing record; other record edits, TXT included, are POSTs to https://freedns.afraid.org/subdomain/save.php with a logged-in session cookie; the interface term for the update URL would be dyndns, which the vocabulary lacks, so interface carries unknown
tooling: curl against sync.afraid.org/u/<token>/; DD-WRT and router integrations
chaining: a free hostname that resolves without owning a domain, which is the only thing here that does

limits.value: 5 free shared-registry hostnames and 20 subdomains on each domain you own
a hostname on a Shared: Private domain can be rejected by that domain's owner, while a Shared: Public domain takes hostnames without the owner's approval
the free plan keeps captchas, which every paid plan removes; the pricing table does not say which actions they guard

identity_cost.detail: a first and last name, a user ID, a password and an e-mail address that receives the activation link, an image captcha, and a required checkbox declaring the user is not on a U.S. restricted list or in a U.S.-sanctioned territory; no phone and no card (https://freedns.afraid.org/signup/)

reliability_note: a shared-registry name is on someone else's domain, so its survival is their decision
confidence_note: the landing, features, pricing, signup, signup Q&A and FAQ pages were read and quoted; the shared-registry cap of 5 hostnames and the 20-subdomain cap on an owned domain are first-party figures

evidence.proved: '23,246 domains in the shared domain registry'; dynamic update by URL token at sync.afraid.org/u/<token>/; free and premium subdomain and domain hosting
the registry is a browsable list of domains a hostname may be attached to
an account may host any number of owned domains; the same page counts 23,097 shared-registry domains

evidence.proved: third party: a ddclient issue ties the /api/ page to the v1 update protocol, which takes one request to get the update URL of a host and one to perform the update
evidence.quote: The [v1 update protocol](https://freedns.afraid.org/api/) is used, which requires two requests: one to get the update URL for the desired host and another to actually perform the update.
